exam_guide_revision: Practical Python data-stack curriculum reviewed against current official NumPy, pandas, Matplotlib, and Seaborn documentation on 2026-09-19.

learning_design.unlock_rule: A knowledge node unlocks after all required prompts are revealed.
learning_design.mastery_note: Discovery progress is not mastery evidence; retrieval questions and typed coding questions provide the scored signal.

authoring_notes: Interactive first-pass learning for Matplotlib. Emphasizes choosing the chart from the analysis question and DataFrame column types before memorizing plotting syntax, then composes object-oriented plotting APIs.

modules.title: Choose plots and reason about the object-oriented workflow

nodes.title: Choose the chart from the question

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Choose the chart from the variable types and the __________ you are asking.

reveal.text: Choose the chart from the variable types and the question you are asking.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Two numeric variables → scatter; ordered time vs numeric → line; category vs magnitude → __________.

reveal.text: Two numeric variables → scatter; ordered time vs numeric → line; category vs magnitude → bar.

prompts.label: 👀 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: One numeric distribution → histogram; compare numeric distributions across categories → __________ plot.

reveal.text: One numeric distribution → histogram; compare numeric distributions across categories → box plot.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `plt.subplots()` returns a Figure and one or more __________.

reveal.text: `plt.subplots()` returns a Figure and one or more Axes.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: A common workflow is `subplots → draw on ax → label ax → legend/layout → __________`.

reveal.text: A common workflow is `subplots → draw on ax → label ax → legend/layout → show`.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Prefer Axes methods like `ax.scatter` and `ax.set_xlabel` when you are managing explicit subplot __________.

reveal.text: Prefer Axes methods like `ax.scatter` and `ax.set_xlabel` when you are managing explicit subplot objects.

nodes.title: Scatter for relationships, line for ordered trends

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `ax.scatter(x, y)` shows individual numeric pairs; `ax.plot(x, y)` emphasizes an __________ sequence.

reveal.text: `ax.scatter(x, y)` shows individual numeric pairs; `ax.plot(x, y)` emphasizes an ordered sequence.

prompts.label: 🎯 WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Age vs income usually suggests scatter; month vs revenue usually suggests a __________ plot.

reveal.text: Age vs income usually suggests scatter; month vs revenue usually suggests a line plot.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: A line can imply continuity/order between adjacent observations, so do not use it for unordered numeric pairs without a meaningful __________.

reveal.text: A line can imply continuity/order between adjacent observations, so do not use it for unordered numeric pairs without a meaningful order.

nodes.title: Bar is categorical magnitude; histogram is a distribution

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `bar` receives category positions/labels and heights; `hist` automatically groups numeric observations into __________.

reveal.text: `bar` receives category positions/labels and heights; `hist` automatically groups numeric observations into bins.

prompts.label: 🎯 WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Region totals → bar; the shape of thousands of income observations → __________.

reveal.text: Region totals → bar; the shape of thousands of income observations → histogram.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: A histogram's x-axis represents numeric ranges, not named __________.

reveal.text: A histogram's x-axis represents numeric ranges, not named categories.

nodes.title: Axes labels and titles make the encoding explicit

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: On an Axes, use `set_xlabel`, `set_ylabel`, and `__________` for the title.

reveal.text: On an Axes, use `set_xlabel`, `set_ylabel`, and `set_title` for the title.

prompts.label: 🎯 WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Labels should tell the learner what variable and, when useful, what __________ the axis represents.

reveal.text: Labels should tell the learner what variable and, when useful, what units the axis represents.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: The `ax.` object-oriented methods use the `set_` prefix; pyplot-level helpers like `plt.xlabel` do __________.

reveal.text: The `ax.` object-oriented methods use the `set_` prefix; pyplot-level helpers like `plt.xlabel` do not.

nodes.title: Legends, reference lines, limits, and grids

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `ax.legend()` displays labels attached to plotted artists with `__________=...`.

reveal.text: `ax.legend()` displays labels attached to plotted artists with `label=...`.

prompts.label: 🎯 WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: `ax.axhline` adds a horizontal reference value such as a target or __________.

reveal.text: `ax.axhline` adds a horizontal reference value such as a target or threshold.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: `set_xlim` changes the visible x-range; it does not filter the underlying __________.

reveal.text: `set_xlim` changes the visible x-range; it does not filter the underlying data.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `plt.subplots(1, 2)` creates one row and __________ columns of Axes.

reveal.text: `plt.subplots(1, 2)` creates one row and two columns of Axes.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: With two side-by-side Axes, the first is commonly addressed as `axes[__________]`.

reveal.text: With two side-by-side Axes, the first is commonly addressed as `axes[0]`.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: A multi-panel figure lets different plots answer __________ questions while sharing one overall presentation.

reveal.text: A multi-panel figure lets different plots answer complementary questions while sharing one overall presentation.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `fig.tight_layout()` adjusts subplot spacing to reduce __________ between labels/titles and neighboring Axes.

reveal.text: `fig.tight_layout()` adjusts subplot spacing to reduce overlap between labels/titles and neighboring Axes.

prompts.label: 🎯 WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Apply layout adjustments after the figure's Axes and labels have been __________.

reveal.text: Apply layout adjustments after the figure's Axes and labels have been created.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: `tight_layout` is a Figure-level layout operation; it is not a data plotting __________.

reveal.text: `tight_layout` is a Figure-level layout operation; it is not a data plotting method.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: A complete small plot is usually `create Axes → choose plot → draw data → label axes/title → optional context → __________`.

reveal.text: A complete small plot is usually `create Axes → choose plot → draw data → label axes/title → optional context → show`.

prompts.label: 🎯 WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Before writing code, identify the DataFrame column types and decide which column maps to x, y, category/color, or __________.

reveal.text: Before writing code, identify the DataFrame column types and decide which column maps to x, y, category/color, or aggregation.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Do not memorize a long plotting block as one unit; each method should correspond to a specific visual __________.

reveal.text: Do not memorize a long plotting block as one unit; each method should correspond to a specific visual intention.
